name: Maine
agency: Maine Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV)
permitAge: 15, enrolled in an approved driver education program, with written parental consent

teen.supervisedHours: 70 hours, including 10 after dark, starting after the permit is issued (under 21)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate license: no passengers other than immediate family unless a qualifying licensed operator is present; restrictions last 270 days (29-A M.R.S. 1311)
teen.phone: Permit holders under 21: no cell phone use. Intermediate under 18: hand-held device only when pulled off the road and stopped. All drivers: no holding a phone while driving since Sept. 2019 (29-A 2121); hands-free allowed.

notes: Supervisor: at least 20 years old, licensed at least 2 years (maine.gov).
Knowledge test: commercial sites say 30 questions, 80 percent (one says 83 percent); not confirmed by BMV, so left null.
Night limit midnight to 5 a.m. appears only in secondary sources (NSC, dmvroads); not confirmed in 29-A 1311 text, so null and not used.

Handbook link is the official study guide page (Driver License Manual PDF and Motorist Handbook); direct PDF URL not confirmed. No Spanish handbook found. A commercial site claims free interpreters for the written test since Feb. 2026; unverified.
Intermediate restrictions extended another 270 days after a violation (29-A 1311).
Move over (29-A 2054): pass in a non-adjacent lane if possible, otherwise at a careful and prudent speed; fines reported vary.
